Title: June 4, 2026 - Boulder City Council and Planning Board Special Joint Meeting
Overview: The council and planning board held a joint public hearing on the recommended major update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan after a staff presentation on the plan's goals, policies, and future land use changes. Members questioned staff on the land use map, industrial and residential uses, housing goals, and notice to property owners, and the public spoke in large numbers, many raising concerns about density and notification. No final vote was taken; planning board will deliberate on June 16 and city council on June 25, 2026, and the council also approved its consent agenda, including a Pride Month proclamation.

Topic1.Title: Pride Month Proclamation
Topic1.Summary: The council presented a declaration recognizing June 2026 as Pride Month, commemorating the Stonewall events and recognizing local LGBTQ plus organizations. A representative of Rocky Mountain Equality accepted the proclamation and thanked the council for its support. The proclamation was part of the consent agenda items the council later approved.

Topic2.Title: Council Statements on Campus Group Letter and Hate Crime Sentencing
Topic2.Summary: A council member used a point of personal privilege to condemn a University of Colorado student group's letter that defended the 2025 attack in Boulder. Another council member read a statement from the District Attorney about the life sentence and the commitment to fighting hate crimes. Both members asked colleagues to join in condemning the statement.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda Approval
Topic3.Summary: The council approved consent agenda items 2A through 2F after a motion and second. The vote was unanimous on a roll call.

Topic4.Title: Staff Presentation on the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Update
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented the recommended major update, which followed about 20 months of engagement and included over a thousand comments on the March draft. The update sets 104 plain-language policies and a simplified future land use strategy with 12 designations, plus a new rural class and revised open space mapping. Staff explained that the plan sets direction over 20 years but does not guarantee specific outcomes, which will depend on future zoning and implementation. The presentation also outlined the four-body approval process and the schedule for county and city deliberations.

Topic5.Title: Questions on Land Use Map Changes, Maintenance Costs, and Wildfire Density
Topic5.Summary: Council and board members asked for a delta map showing land use changes since the last draft, and staff agreed to prepare one for the June 16 meeting. A member asked for stronger plan language on funding long-term facility and infrastructure maintenance and on prioritizing affordable housing. Staff said the plan already elevates asset maintenance in policy 20 and funding stability in policy 64. Staff also confirmed that increasing density in neighborhood one near wildfire-prone areas would require zoning changes and evacuation review first.

Topic6.Title: Amendment Procedure and Timing
Topic6.Summary: Staff explained that amendments must come from each body and must be specific, substantive changes rather than minor wording edits. Any change made by one body would require the other bodies to review it, possibly adding meetings into July, August, or September. The city attorney advised that planning board should submit suggestions through staff rather than through a chain of emails to avoid creating a public meeting outside the agenda.

Topic7.Title: Industrial Land and Residential Uses
Topic7.Summary: Members asked whether residential uses are prohibited in industrial designations and whether the change would affect existing industrial tenants. Staff said residential is not described in the industrial classes but zoning still governs what is allowed, and that the revised plan aims to shift housing to other areas. Staff acknowledged that current use review does not offer strong protections for existing industrial tenants. Members said they would raise further questions at the June 16 meeting.

Topic8.Title: Affordable Housing Goal and Implementation Direction
Topic8.Summary: A member questioned why the plan keeps a 15 percent affordable housing goal that may not be achievable by 2035. The housing director said the goal was intentionally aspirational and that the city should aim high. Staff said the citywide strategic plan and two-year council priority setting will provide implementation direction, and a suggestion was made to clarify the hierarchy of plans in the document.

Topic9.Title: Sub-Community Planning, Planning Reserve, and Groundwater
Topic9.Summary: Members asked how sub-community and area planning guidance will be handled after being moved out of the plan into operational guidance. Staff said the existing process continues and that new sub-community plans will be developed and vetted with the boards. Staff also said the planning reserve process will be revisited through the intergovernmental agreement, which runs through 2042. Members also asked about groundwater protection, and staff said the state regulates groundwater and the city does not.

Topic10.Title: Public Hearing Testimony
Topic10.Summary: Seventeen people signed up, each with two minutes, and speakers raised concerns about density, housing types, water supply, wildfire evacuation, and the survey design. The Boulder Chamber and a former planning board member urged restoring language allowing residential uses in industrial areas. Several speakers said residents were not properly notified about proposed land use changes and called for individual letters. Others supported the 15-minute neighborhood concept and asked for affordable housing requirements tied to upzoning.

Topic11.Title: Clarifying Questions on Notification and Survey Methods
Topic11.Summary: Staff explained that property owners were notified through utility billing because mailing about 55,000 letters was impractical, and the city attorney said the notice complied with legal requirements. Staff said a national survey consultant reviewed and finalized the survey questions to make them statistically valid. Staff also clarified that outreach was open to all residents and was not specifically targeted at university students.

Topic12.Title: Motions to Continue the Hearing
Topic12.Summary: The planning board voted seven to zero to continue the item to June 16, 2026, for deliberation and action. The council then unanimously voted to continue its deliberation and action on the plan to June 25, 2026. Both bodies noted that no additional public comment would be taken at those deliberation meetings, though emails would still be read.
